newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to launch new world rubber pact Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to launch new world rubber pact Tuesday.

text.p: Malaysia will launch a new world rubber price pact on Tuesday, concluding more than a year of uncertainty on an agreement which brings together producers and consumers, officials said on Monday.

The International Natural Rubber Agreement 3 (INRA 3) will be launched by Malaysian Primary Industries Minister Lim Keng Yaik in Kuala Lumpur, in a ceremony to be witnessed by UN officials and key people in the global rubber industry.
"The launch will be followed by the first series of council meetings under the INRA 3," said an official of the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO), which will administer the pact.
The INRA 3, a U.N.-brokered pact, is the world's only remaining global commodity agreement with economic provisions and a buffer stock that allows for buying and selling to stabilise prices.

Two cycles of the agreement -- INRA 1 and INRA 2 -- have been completed, but the third was held over for over a year due to delays in getting at least 75 percent of rubber producers and importers to sign and ratify the pact.

The main problem was a tussle between Malaysia and Indonesia for the post of executive director. The dispute was finally solved in February when Indonesia gave way to Malaysia's candidate, Ahmad Zubeir Noordin.

Ahmad Zubeir, the deputy secretary-general of Malaysia's Primary Industries Ministry, will be officially appointed to his new position at Tuesday's first council meeting of the INRA 3, the INRO official told Reuters.
He said the rest of the agenda mainly involved administrative matters concerning the transition of INRA 2 to INRA 3.

The outgoing executive director, Pong Sono of Thailand, the chairman of the International Natural Rubber Council, James McGlinchey, and a representative of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) will also be speaking at the launching.
